overview: 23 official Group 1 Prelims questions (2010–2024). E-governance schemes lead (9 Qs); basics of ICT, ICT in daily life and ICT in industry give about 4 each; cyber security 2; netiquette never asked. Early papers were one-liners (full forms, first-ever facts); 2023–24 switch to statement-based, negative and assertion-reason items on India Stack, e-RUPI, RFID, blockchain and Indian AI models.

possibility.angle: Nature and scope of ICT: hardware basics, networks, full forms
possibility.what_they_ask: material of ICs (silicon), which country built a supercomputer, IPv4 vs IPv6 bit length, full form (Li-Fi)

possibility.angle: ICT in day-to-day life: digital wallets, m-health, AI in health
possibility.what_they_ask: first-ever (computer-literate panchayat, digital wallet), term for mobile health, who developed an AI health model and what it measures

possibility.angle: ICT and industry: RFID, blockchain, Indian AI products
possibility.what_they_ask: how a technology works (passive/active RFID power, blockchain control), which company/consortium launched an AI tool (Hanooman, Pratham)

possibility.angle: ICT and governance: e-governance missions, platforms, payments
possibility.what_they_ask: name of a mission/portal (e-Kranti, GeM), which body runs it (NITI Aayog, NPCI, NCRB, DoT), launch year (e-RUPI 2021), state project's function (Khajane vs Bhoomi), layers of India Stack

possibility.angle: Cyber security and National Cyber Security Policy
possibility.what_they_ask: first computer virus (Creeper), which state's system was attacked; NCSP 2013 goals, CERT-In role and the IT Act are the natural next targets

possibility.evidence: 0 official Qs; not seen in the related sample either
possibility.what_they_ask: likely definitional: meaning of netiquette, flaming, spamming, writing in capitals = shouting, cyber-bullying – asked like the full-form items

traps.spot: a dated statement in an otherwise true scheme description
traps.fix: Pin launch years: e-RUPI 2 Aug 2021; RBI's e-rupee CBDC pilot 2022

traps.trap: Implementing body swapped to the obvious IT ministry
traps.spot: a policing/security system attributed to NIC/MeitY
traps.fix: Ask whose job it is: facial recognition for police = NCRB under MHA
traps.pyq: 'NAFRS … developed by NIC under MeitY' → NCRB, MHA [group1-prelims-2023-paper2#62]

traps.trap: Function swapped between two projects of the same state
traps.spot: state project names (Khajane, Bhoomi) with a function
traps.fix: Karnataka: Bhoomi = land records; Khajane = treasury

traps.trap: Properties swapped between categories of a technology
traps.fix: Passive: no battery, reader-powered; active: own battery; semi-passive: battery for chip, replies via reader waves
traps.pyq: 'Passive RFID tags powered by an internal circuit' → reader-powered [group1-prelims-2023-paper2#72]

traps.spot: a statement restricting a general-purpose technology to its famous use
traps.fix: Check whether the technology works outside that use: blockchain stores any data, not only cryptocurrency

traps.trap: Wrong count and wrong layer in a Reason
traps.spot: A-R where R gives a number of layers and credits one layer
traps.fix: India Stack = 3 layers; e-KYC savings come from the identity (Aadhaar) layer, not payments
traps.pyq: 'two interconnected layers … Payment Layer reduced e-KYC cost' → A true, R false [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#71]

traps.spot: options compare two versions of a standard
traps.pyq: IPv4 vs IPv6 → IPv4 needs fewer bits [group1-prelims-2019-paper2#69]

techniques.name: [E19/4] Mandate test for 'who runs it'
techniques.how: Classify the scheme (payments, policing, procurement, telecom), then pick the body whose mandate fits; strike generic IT bodies unless the job is IT itself.
techniques.example: 'Sangam: Digital Twin' is a telecom initiative → naval commands and DST fall → Department of Telecommunications [group1-prelims-2024-paper2#114]

techniques.name: Number-and-layer audit for A-R
techniques.how: Check every number in A and R separately; a wrong count makes R false even when A is true.
techniques.example: India Stack has three layers, R says two → R false; A true → '(A) true, (R) false' [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#71]

techniques.name: Prefix logic for e-/m-/i- terms
techniques.how: The prefix names the channel: m = mobile/wireless, e = electronic in general; match the stem's channel.
techniques.example: stem lists SMS, apps, wearables → mobile → m-health [group1-prelims-2019-paper2#71]

techniques.name: Mechanism reasoning for technology statements
techniques.how: Ask how the technology physically works; a statement that contradicts the mechanism is false even if worded confidently.
techniques.example: RFID uses radio waves → no line of sight needed (IV true); active means own battery (III false) → II and IV only [group1-prelims-2023-paper2#72]

techniques.name: Odd-one-out by objective
techniques.how: In a list of genuine schemes, test each against the exact objective in the stem; drop any with a different target group or stage.
techniques.example: e-RUPI: one-time voucher, NPCI, DFS + NHA true; launch 2020 false → I, II and III only [group1-prelims-2023-paper2#103]

confusions.remember: e-RUPI = NPCI purpose-specific voucher on UPI; e₹ = RBI's central bank digital currency
Karnataka: Bhoomi = land records; Khajane = treasury
e-Kranti = NeGP 2.0, electronic delivery of all services; e-Biz = business-licence portal
GeM = one-stop e-marketplace for government buying (2016)
Passive = no battery, reader-powered; active = own battery, longer range
Li-Fi = Light Fidelity: data over visible light
Crime/facial-recognition databases = NCRB; government IT backbone = NIC

confusions.b: Elk Cloner (first in the wild on PCs, 1982)

confusions.remember: Hanooman = BharatGPT + SML, 11 languages; Krutrim = Ola; Bhashini = MeitY translation mission
DARPAN = project-monitoring dashboard; PRAGATI = pro-active governance and timely implementation; e-Pragati = AP's state enterprise architecture

anchors: India Stack = 3 layers: identity (Aadhaar/e-KYC), payments (UPI), data (DigiLocker/consent)
e-RUPI launched 2 Aug 2021 – NPCI with DFS, MoHFW and NHA
GeM – government e-marketplace for goods and services
e-Kranti – electronic delivery of all government services (NeGP 2.0)
NAFRS – NCRB, Ministry of Home Affairs
Garbhini-GA2 – fetal age, IIT Madras + THSTI Faridabad
MobiKwik – keyed first digital wallet company in India
Hanooman – multimodal AI in 11 Indian languages (BharatGPT + SML)
checklist: Name the body whose mandate fits the scheme before reading options.
Check every year and number in scheme statements.
For technology statements, test against how the technology works.
In A-R, judge R's numbers and attribution separately from A.
State e-gov names: recall the state and the function together.
